paper.title: Explore no more: Improved high-probability regret bounds for non-stochastic bandits

unmapped: regret is the actual (realised) regret, bounded with high probability
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the two players interact as follows: The learner picks an \emph{arm} $I_t\in[K]$ and the environment selects a loss function $\loss_t: [K] \ra [0,1]$... Subsequently, the learner incurs and observes the loss $\loss_{t,I_t}$.

unmapped: N experts give probabilistic advice over K arms each round; regret measured against best expert
settings.definition_quote: the learner observes a set of $N$ probability distributions $\bxp_{t}(1),\dots,\bxp_{t}(N)\in[0,1]^K$ over the $K$ arms... The goal of the learner in this setting is to pick a sequence of arms so as to minimize the regret against the best expert

settings.name_in_paper: Tracking the best sequence of arms
unmapped: regret against best comparator sequence switching at most S times (switching comparator, environment itself is arbitrary adversarial)
learner knows S (number of comparator switches)
settings.definition_quote: we consider the class of sequences that switch at most $S$ times between actions. We measure the performance of the learner in this setting in terms of the regret against the best sequence from this class $C(S)\subseteq[K]^T$

unmapped: fixed directed feedback graph G; learner knows independence number of G for tuning
settings.definition_quote: The structure of the side observations is described by the directed graph $G$: nodes of $G$ correspond to individual arms, and the presence of arc $i\ra j$ implies that the learner will observe $\loss_{t,j}$ upon selecting $I_t = i$.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$. With $\eta_t = 2\gamma_t = \sqrt{\frac{2\log K}{KT}}$ for all $t$, \exphix guarantees $R_T \le 2\sqrt{2KT\log K} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\log K}} + 1} \log\pa{2/\delta}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Holds for all delta simultaneously (parameters don't depend on delta).

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Furthermore, setting $\eta_t = 2\gamma_t = \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{Kt}}$ for all $t$, the bound becomes $R_T \le 4\sqrt{KT\log K} + \pa{2\sqrt{\frac{KT}{\log K}} +1 } \log\pa{2/\delta}$.

results.notes: Anytime version, no knowledge of T.

source.label: thm:experts
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{2\log N}{KT}}$ for all $t$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \expnix satisfies $R_T^\xi \le 2\sqrt{2KT\log N} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\log N}} +1 }\log\pa{2/\delta}$.

symbols.S_sw: maximum number of switches of the comparator sequence (paper's S); bar S = S+1

extra_assumptions: eta = 2 gamma = sqrt(2 bar S log K/(KT)), alpha = S/(T-1)

source.label: thm:tracking
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{2\bar{S}\log K }{KT}}$ and $\alpha = \frac{S}{T-1}$, where $\bar{S} = S + 1$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \exphsix satisfies $R_T^S \le 2\sqrt{2KT\bar{S}\log \pa{\frac{eKT}{S}}} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\bar{S}\log K}} + 1} \log\pa{2/\delta}$.

results.notes: Regret against best S-switching sequence; recorded as switching_regret.

symbols.alpha_G: independence number of the feedback graph G

extra_assumptions: eta = 2 gamma = sqrt(log K/(2 alpha T log(KT))), requires knowledge of alpha_G and T

source.label: thm:sideobs
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$. Assume that $T\ge K^2/(8\alpha)$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{2\alpha T \log(KT)}}$, where $\alpha$ is the \emph{independence number} of $G$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, \exphix guarantees R_T \le ...

results.notes: Interpreted 'log KT' as log(K*T). Algorithm proposed by Kocak et al. 2014; high-prob bound is new.
